dedupe_keys.name: hospital disaster resilience in a tertiary hospital after the 2015 nepal earthquake

description: This case study looks at how a tertiary hospital in Nepal coped with the 2015 earthquake, as part of a doctoral dissertation on hospital resilience that was summarised in Global Health Action. It combines routinely generated hospital admission records, analysed with advanced statistical methods, with semi-structured interviews of hospital staff, coded both inductively and deductively. Most earthquake victims admitted needed surgery and long stays, which strained the hospital; for six weeks daily admissions fell, injury cases made up a large and long-staying share, and other admissions fell and were shorter. The hospital's resilience depended on adaptations that emerged during the crisis as well as on its disaster plan, and on the individual resilience of staff, shaped by their sense of safety, meaning and belonging. Coverage: one tertiary hospital in Nepal. Access: free open-access article. Licence: CC BY. Caveats: one hospital; the hospital records themselves are not published. Simulation uses are surge and length-of-stay parameters for hospital capacity models after earthquakes, and evidence for how staff adaptations change recovery. Related records: the PAHO hospital safety index and the Pathfinder egress model used for hospital evacuation studies.
